lesson.title: Questions à la Française
lesson.subtitle: Three ladders of asking: rising voice, est-ce que, and inversion — plus cognate question words

hook.title: Three Ways to Ask the Exact Same Question
hook.content: English forces you to haul in 'do/does/did' and scramble word order just to ask a question. French gives you a three-rung register ladder instead: Rung 1 is pure rising voice (Tu veux le café ?). Rung 2 snaps the question-opener est-ce que ('is it that') onto the front without moving a single word (Est-ce que tu veux le café ?). Rung 3 flips verb and pronoun for formal polish (Veux-tu le café ?).

footnotes.title: Why pourquoi is English 'wherefore'
footnotes.content: When Juliet asks 'Wherefore art thou Romeo?', she is not asking where he is — she is asking WHY ('for what') he bears that name. French pourquoi is built the exact same way: pour ('for') + quoi ('what')!

pattern.title: Question Word + est-ce que + Statement
pattern.content: When you add a question word — où ('where', cousin of ubiquitous), quand ('when'), comment ('how'), combien ('how much'), or pourquoi ('why') — you can slot it right in front of est-ce que and keep normal statement word order: Où est-ce que tu vas ? Pourquoi est-ce que tu veux partir ? Quand est-ce que le train arrive ? And to answer pourquoi ('for what'), use parce que ('by that which' = because).
pattern.linguist_note: est-ce que grammaticalized from 'is it [the case] that...', allowing French to preserve strict Subject-Verb-Object order even inside wh-questions.
pattern.trap_note: The shortcut your mind will offer: confusing pourquoi ('why?') with parce que ('because'). Remember: quoi at the end of pourquoi is 'what?' — it always asks the question!

exercises.prompt: Match each French question word with its meaning and etymological clue:
exercises.target_answer: où, pourquoi, parce que, quand, combien
exercises.meaning: where (Latin ubi → ubiquitous), why (for-what), because (by-that-which), when (Latin quando), how much / how many
exercises.explanation: où wears a grave accent to distinguish it from ou ('or'); pourquoi asks and parce que answers.

exercises.prompt: What is the literal word-for-word structure of 'Où est-ce que tu es'?
exercises.meaning: Literal structure: Where is-it that you are
exercises.explanation: est-ce que is literally 'is-it that', letting tu es stay in statement order.

exercises.prompt: How do you answer 'Pourquoi tu veux partir ?' ('Why do you want to leave?') with 'Because it is late'?

exercises.idea: you are asking a friend where the café is
cues: Where → Où (with the grave accent ù)
exercises.explanation: Short questions with être simply invert: Où est le café ?

diagnosis.slip: forgot the accent or word order
diagnosis.cue: Start with Où + est + le café.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Pourquoi est-ce que tu veux partir
exercises.target_answer: Pourquoi est-ce que tu veux partir
exercises.meaning: Why do you want to leave?
exercises.explanation: Pourquoi + est-ce que lets tu veux partir stay untouched.
exercises.affirmation: You chained Pourquoi and est-ce que without scrambling the verb.

summary.outcome: Ask questions across all three French registers and pair où, pourquoi, quand, comment, combien with est-ce que.

use_example.german: Pourquoi est-ce que tu es ici ? — Parce que je veux te voir.
use_example.english: Why are you here? — Because I want to see you.

summary.takeaway: est-ce que is your universal question adapter: snap it after any question word and keep normal sentence order.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([701] Est-ce que Drills): see how Questions à la Française leads directly into Est-ce que Drills.

twist.prompt: Ungraded — ask 'When do you want to confirm?' using est-ce que:
twist.target_answer: Quand est-ce que tu veux confirmer
twist.explanation: Quand + est-ce que + tu veux confirmer — zero word-order inversion needed.

foreshadow.line: Having mastered Questions à la Française, look ahead to Topic 8 (The -eur Bridge), where this machinery expands into the next dimension of French thought.

payoff.text: The foundation from Topic 6 (The -ité & -ance Bridges) now pays off directly inside Questions à la Française: every sentence here builds on that earlier step.

est_ce_que.context_phrase: Est-ce que tu veux le gâteau ?
est_ce_que.etymology_derivation: Literally 'is it that you want…' — a question scaffolded out of a statement, no word order changed.

où.etymology_derivation: Latin ubi 'where' — the root English borrowed wholesale in 'ubiquitous' (present everywhere).

pourquoi.etymology_derivation: pour + quoi = 'for what' — English's 'wherefore' (for-what) built the same way: wherefore art thou.

quand.etymology_derivation: Latin quandō. In liaison before a vowel, the d sounds like /t/: quand il arrive /kɑ̃.t‿il/.

combien.etymology_derivation: When followed by a noun, takes bare de: combien de temps ('how much time').

quel.etymology_derivation: Agrees with its noun: quel (m), quelle (f), quels (mpl), quelles (fpl) — all four sound identical (/kɛl/)!

parce_que.etymology_derivation: Pourquoi asks 'for what?'; parce que answers 'by that which'.
